correctness.rationale: An exact q-by-q difference-matrix calculation distinguishes all ordered replacements by row/column sums. The only two-context collision for each ordered replacement is (a,c)=(b,d) versus (d,b). Boundary substitutions contribute disjoint 2(q-1) vectors. For q>=3 each trigram supports a mutation-change vector unique to it, forcing q^3 distinct windows for saturation; an order-three linear de Bruijn word has exactly those windows. BEST and directed Matrix-Tree on the de Bruijn graph count all shortest maximizers. The attached local, literal-enumeration and determinant checkers reproduce q=2..8 (with q>=3 threshold) and q=2..5 counting cases. Finite checks are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The source-substitution dinucleotide-profile ball is a natural loss-of-order observation channel for mutation-corrupted short reads. The exact worst-case cardinality across all q>=3, the optimal first length q^3+2, and exact enumeration of all shortest extremal sources are mathematically motivated invariants describing the channel’s full local diversity and its de Bruijn rigidity, not a trivial global-profile census or a renaming of deletion bounds.
